page: UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-8GB is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Starter family, operating on KVM virtualization. The configuration allocates 2 shared x86_64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, backed by 64 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. It incorporates vector instruction extensions including AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators such as AES and SHA-NI. Hardware resources include 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per vCPU, alongside a bundled 40 GB local SSD and one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated graphics processors are included in this profile.

Benchmark results show sharp contrasts between single-threaded efficiency and parallel capacity. The server achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core execution (3877.27) as well as single-threaded data compression, reaching 41.73 GB/sec in gzip and 17.93 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. However, overall multi-core performance is limited by the two-vCPU shared allocation, reflected in an average stress-ng multi-core score of 7616.6 and weak multi-core results in Geekbench (3225.0) and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression (36.3 GB/sec). Memory and database benchmarks also place in lower percentiles, with PassMark memory scoring 1288.78 and Redis SET throughput reaching 5.88 million operations per second.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio and bundled local storage, this profile delivers cost-effective resource density for low-intensity operations without requiring overprovisioned compute. The presence of shared vCPUs introduces vulnerability to resource contention under prolonged sustained loads, making it suboptimal for heavy multi-threaded data processing, large language model inference, or demanding database servers. It is well aligned with lightweight web serving, development sandboxes, basic microservices, background task workers, and staging environments.
description: UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-8GB is an entry-tier general-purpose virtual instance based on KVM virtualization. It features 2 shared x86_64 vCPUs sourced from an AMD EPYC 9575F processor operating at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 8.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per core) and 40 GB of bundled local SSD storage. The CPU architecture supports advanced vector instruction sets including AVX-512. Benchmarking demonstrates top-tier single-threaded compute and compression throughput, evidenced by 41.73 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput and memory-bound operations exhibit lower performance percentiles, reflecting the constraints of a two-core shared profile. The balanced ratio of memory to compute makes this server cost efficient for baseline utility, making it suitable for staging environments, low-traffic web applications, lightweight microservices, and modest background task processing.
